t: Stalin developed the doctrine of socialism in one country from December 1924, holding that socialism could be completed in Russia without a spreading world revolution, and used it against Trotsky’s permanent revolution.

The Stalinist state carried out the Great Purge, dekulakisation, the gulag system and mass deportations; Soviet archives show nearly 700,000 executions in 1937 and 1938, and the emergent scholarly consensus is that around 1.5 to 1.7 million died in the gulag system from 1930 to 1953.
Historians disagree on whether Stalinism grew out of Leninism: Richard Pipes called it the natural consequence of Leninism, while Roy Medvedev and Graeme Gill saw a break from it.
dyk: In 1936 Stalin told the journalist Roy W. Howard that the export of revolution was “nonsense”, yet a few years earlier he had turned the Soviet economy from the New Economic Policy to a planned economy in what became known as the Great Turn.
ev: Stalin first develops the idea of socialism in one country, elaborating it in his writings of 1925–26
The Soviet famine of 1930–1933 begins during forced collectivisation, and the Holodomor follows near the end of 1932
The Great Terror begins in September, with Nikolai Yezhov heading the NKVD, and the Moscow Trials run to 1938
The History of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union (Bolsheviks) alters the history of the party and of its leaders
Trotsky is assassinated in Mexico, the last of Stalin’s opponents among the former party leadership
Mass deportations of whole peoples begin, and by 1949 nearly 3.3 million people are deported
Stalin dies on 5 March and de-Stalinization follows
Khrushchev’s Secret Speech condemns Stalin’s cult of personality at the Twentieth Party Congress

f.thinkers: Joseph Stalin, who developed socialism in one country; Lazar Kaganovich, who reportedly proposed replacing “Long Live Leninism” with “Long Live Stalinism”; Nikolai Bukharin, whose Right Opposition was defeated; Leon Trotsky, its foremost critic, who promoted permanent revolution; Nikita Khrushchev, who denounced it in 1956; Enver Hoxha, whose Hoxhaism kept a version of it in Albania
f.texts: Stalin’s writings of 1925–26 on socialism in one country; Foundations of Leninism (1924); Economic Problems of Socialism in the USSR (1951); History of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union (Bolsheviks) (1938); Trotsky’s The Stalin School of Falsification and Stalinism and Bolshevism (1937); Khrushchev’s Secret Speech (1956)
f.ideas: socialism in one country; a proletarian state that grows stronger before it withers away; intensification of class conflict; rapid industrialisation under a planned economy; forced collectivisation of agriculture; the party as the leading vanguard of communist revolution; the cult of personality; ideological orthodoxy in science and the arts
f.today: De-Stalinization began in the Soviet Union in the 1950s and 1960s, and most communist parties abandoned Stalinism after 1956, except those of the German Democratic Republic and the Socialist Republic of Romania; Albania under Enver Hoxha stayed committed to its brand of Stalinism for decades; historians still dispute whether Stalinism followed from Leninism
